audit.whatIsWrong: Devour is called his W in five strings — "his W Devour", "W Devour reset", "W Devour you or a minion" — and the full layer builds its entire tracked-ability apparatus around Abyssal Dive described as "His escape + shield" (tldr, winCon, focus, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], phases[1].why). Separately, the grey health is credited to his passive in six strings.
audit.why: Three slots are wrong at once. Devour is R, not W. Abyssal Dive is W and it is neither an escape nor a shield — Riot's text is "Dive down and then re-appear at target location, damaging and knocking up all enemies in an area", a 21s knockup at rank 1. And the grey health is Thick Skin (E): "Passive: Tahm Kench stores a percent of the damage he takes and heals based on it while out of combat. Active: Convert all stored damage into a temporary shield." His actual passive, An Acquired Taste, gives bonus damage from total health and builds the stacks. So the page tells the reader to track a shield that does not exist on an ability that does something else entirely.
audit.corrected: Devour returned to R, Abyssal Dive restated as a 21s knockup dive, and the grey health attributed to Thick Skin across both layers.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (P, W cd 21/20/19/18/17, E cd 3, R)

audit.whatIsWrong: The stack economy is never stated. spikes[0] says "three stacks stun" and other strings treat Devour as a separate threat to be waited out, so the reader is told to fear the stun AND the eat simultaneously.
audit.why: Riot's Tongue Lash text: "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." And An Acquired Taste: "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion." Both spend the same three stacks, so he gets one or the other, never both. That single fact replaces every vague "hold R until his Devour is down" instruction with a countable resource sitting on the reader's own health bar — commit at two stacks or fewer and neither answer is available. The already-audited mirror file reached the same conclusion from Tahm Kench's side, so both pages now teach the same rule.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[0], spikes[1], spikes[2], early, mid, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], whys[3], whys[4], tldr, winCon, focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dontsFull[0] and report[5].
sources: audits/top/tahmkench__ambessa.json (mirror, same finding from his side)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], mid and whys[3] credit Public Execution with "R's flat armor pen and on-hit healing" / "the flat armor pen plus on-ability healing" / "the armor pen plus healing".
audit.why: Public Execution blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. No penetration and no healing. Against a champion whose entire design is out-lasting you, an invented heal is the claim most likely to get the reader killed, and it is exactly the sustain race Tahm Kench wants. The mirror file flagged the same fabricated heal from the other side.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the crash stun as the reason the follow-up lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] recommends anti-heal with the generic reason "his healing fights your pattern", and no string anywhere says what heals or how often.
audit.why: Two separate sources, both worth naming. Tongue Lash "heal[s] himself if he strikes an enemy champion" on a 7s cooldown at rank 1, so every poke he lands is a heal on a clock the reader can count. Thick Skin "heals based on" stored damage while out of combat, which is why backing off resets him to full. _missing-interactions.json flags this pair for needs-antiheal and it is a true positive — it just needed the mechanism attached.
audit.corrected: Both healing sources named with the 7s cooldown in report[8], late and dosFull[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The whys[] array is off by one stage from level 4 onward. whys[3] sits under "Levels 4-5" but describes Public Execution, which does not exist until 6; whys[4] sits under "Level 6" but describes the Eclipse first-item spike; whys[5] sits under "First item" and opens "Trades nine and beyond net even". phases[1].why also repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield" error.
audit.why: Same defect found in the Rumble entry for this champion, so it is probably systematic rather than a one-off. A reader at level 4 is told to use an ultimate they will not have for two levels. All three stages have real content available: 4-5 is Ambessa's longest cooldowns against a 7s Tongue Lash, 6 is Public Execution, and first item is Eclipse plus Q max.
audit.corrected: whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] shifted back onto their own stages; phases[1].why corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagrees with its own whys[] at five of seven stages: Skill at level 1 where whys[0] says "the lane opens his", Tahm Kench at levels 2 and 3 where whys[1] says "it nets even" and whys[2] says "it stays a skill tie", and Skill at levels 4-5 and 6 where the packet and the mirror both give Ambessa the level-6 window.
audit.why: At 48.34% over 302 games Ambessa is slightly behind overall, with a real window in the middle. The packet levelChart is Tahm Kench, Skill, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Skill, Tahm Kench, and the already-audited mirror agrees that level 6 belongs to Ambessa — its whys[4] reads "Devour is live now, but Public Execution answers it". The two pages must not disagree on that stage.
audit.corrected: Not changed. "Tahm Kench" is 10 characters against "Skill" 5 and "Ambessa" 7, so every flip crosses the length band by a wide margin. The prose has been aligned to the mirror instead, so the two pages agree in text. Documented in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1], dosFull[2] and all three dontsFull descriptions are stock boilerplate unrelated to their titles, and dontsFull[1] is titled "Fight into his W reactivate" when the reactivation belongs to Thick Skin (E).
audit.why: The title itself carries the slot error, so fixing only the description would leave the page pointing at the wrong ability. Each entry has a concrete answer: Tongue Lash reaches 900 and heals on hit, Abyssal Dive is his one long cooldown, the third stack consumes all three, Thick Skin converts on demand, and An Acquired Taste scales his damage off his own health.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].t repointed to Thick Skin and all five descriptions rewritten against the kit.

edits.before: Tahm's Q tongue slows you and stacks his passive — three stacks stun, and his grey-health passive shrugs off the single ability you can cast back, so don't trade into a free Q.
edits.after: Tongue Lash slows, heals him off you, and stacks An Acquired Taste — at three stacks he can stun you with Q or eat you with Devour, never both. Watch the count, not his cooldowns.

edits.before: Public Execution blinks you behind him and suppresses him in place; with R's flat armor pen and on-hit healing, your Q1-auto-Q2 finally beats his grey bar — but only if his W Devour is down so he can't eat the suppress and reset.
edits.after: Public Execution blinks to him and suppresses him in place, and the crash stun holds him for the follow-up. The number that decides it is his stack count on you: at three he answers with Devour, so commit at two or fewer.

edits.after: Eclipse plus your Q-max chunk is your cleanest window — force the all-in while he sits under three stacks and Thick Skin's stored damage is already spent.

edits.before: Tahm's grey-health passive is the whole problem early — your single Level 1 ability and your Level 2 Q+E barely dent him because the damage just becomes grey health he heals back the moment you stop hitting. Do NOT walk up to free-cast a Q he can answer: his tongue (Q) slows you and stacks his passive, and once it stuns mid-trade it cancels your Drakehound dash and strands you in his range. Farm with the doubled outer edge of Cunning Sweep, accept you can't kill through grey health yet, and don't burn E chasing a drain tank who out-sustains your chip.
edits.after: Thick Skin is the whole problem early — your single Level 1 ability and your Level 2 Q+E barely dent him, because the stored damage becomes a shield on demand and heals him back out of combat. Do NOT walk up to free-cast a Q he can answer: Tongue Lash reaches 900, slows you, heals him off the hit, and stacks An Acquired Taste. The third stack is the one that matters — Q consumes it for a stun that cancels your Drakehound dash. Farm with the doubled outer edge of Cunning Sweep and count your stacks.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your worst window — your cooldowns are longest and his grey health plus W Devour reset means he wins any extended trade you start, so wait for 6. Your R (Public Execution) is the one moment that flips this: it blinks you behind him, suppresses him in place, and the flat armor pen plus on-ability healing finally lets your burst beat his grey bar — but ONLY if his W Devour is down, or he just survives the suppress and Devours back to full. Bait the Devour, then R; never R into a fresh one.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your worst window — your cooldowns are longest and Thick Skin plus Devour means he wins any extended trade you start, so wait for 6. Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1 and knocks up, so it is the one long cooldown worth baiting. Your R is the moment that flips this: Public Execution blinks to him, suppresses him in place, and the crash stun holds him through the follow-up. Time it by his stack count, not by a cooldown — at three stacks he chooses the Q stun or the Devour, so commit while you carry one or two.

edits.before: This stays his lane long-term. His grey-health passive scales with his max HP and your damage is entirely physical, so every drawn-out fight refills the bar you just emptied — and once he stacks health items he simply out-lasts your combo. Your only real edge is tempo: hit your Eclipse and Q-max spike, win the 6-and-first-item window hard, and cash that lead before his R roams turn the map. If it goes 25+ minutes even, he wins by not dying.
edits.after: This stays his lane long-term. Thick Skin scales with the damage he takes and your damage is entirely physical, so every drawn-out fight refills the bar you just emptied — and once he stacks health items he simply out-lasts your combo. Tongue Lash heals him off every poke too, which is why Grievous Wounds is core rather than optional. Your only edge is tempo: win the 6-and-first-item window hard and cash it before he stops dying.

notes:
MIRROR REUSED: audits/top/tahmkench__ambessa.json already existed and I took its central finding rather than re-deriving it — three An Acquired Taste stacks buy the Tongue Lash stun OR the Devour, never both, because Q consumes the stacks Devour needs. Both pages now state the same rule from their own side, and both give level 6 to Ambessa. The mirror also independently caught the same fabricated "heal-on-ability" on Public Execution, which is more evidence that string is a champion-wide problem rather than a local typo.

ONE DISAGREEMENT WITH THE MIRROR I DID NOT PROPAGATE: the mirror's breakdown.cooldowns states "Devour: 120s". champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json reports Devour's cooldown as 0, which is what Data Dragon carries for a stack-gated ability. Rather than assert either figure I wrote no cooldown for Devour at all and gated it on the stack count, which is true under both readings. Worth resolving before either page quotes a number.

THREE SLOT ERRORS, all in one entry: Devour called W (it is R) five times, Abyssal Dive called an "escape + shield" when it is a 21s knockup dive, and the grey health credited to his passive when it is Thick Skin (E). The full layer's whole tracking apparatus — tldr, winCon, focus, both do-strings, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5] — pointed at Abyssal Dive as the ability to wait out, which is neither what it does nor the thing that decides the lane.

STAGE MISALIGNMENT, second occurrence for this champion: whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] each describe the stage after the one they sit under, so level 4-5 readers are told to use an ultimate they do not have. The Rumble entry has the identical off-by-one. Worth checking champ-data/content/ambessa.js for others.

COULD NOT FIT IN THE BAND, for the user to apply by hand: the whole level chart. Content win[] and full phases[].side should read Tahm Kench, Skill, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Skill, Tahm Kench, matching the packet and the mirror. "Tahm Kench" is 10 characters against "Skill" 5 and "Ambessa" 7, so nothing is within +/-10%.
